subject: physical-education
title: Performance task build: weather and hydration
essentialQuestion: How can understanding outdoor recreation and navigation help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

lessonFamilyPlan.instructionalPurpose: build a bounded plan that transfers the target to an accessible setting
lessonFamilyPlan.guidedEmphasis: Stage the access check, setup, safe simulation or description, evidence choice, and finish before combining the plan.
lessonFamilyPlan.independentEvidence: Complete a fresh safe simulation or described plan with honest scope and guardian authority where required.
lessonFamilyPlan.evidencePurpose: planning, decision quality, application, reflection, and completion

goal: I can build a bounded plan that transfers the target to an accessible setting for weather and hydration, using a safe standard or equal-credit adapted route, and explain the cue or decision that shows success.
successOverview: Success is safe setup, use of the taught Scan, plan, pace, turn back. cue or decision, a fresh bounded application, and a short explanation. Credit never depends on body position, speed, athletic talent, comparison, or use of the standard route.
readinessCheck: Identify the safest start, boundary, and turnaround on a simple supplied route.
Choose movement, seated, supported, mobility-aid, low-space, no-equipment, or described evidence without explaining why.
Use the complete described route if guardian permission, safe space, equipment, movement, a partner, or a real setting is unavailable.
materials: Optional: paper map, weather-appropriate clothing, or activity-specific safety equipment when available and guardian-approved.
Use a hand-drawn route, imaginary landmarks, or soft household markers indoors.
movementCues: SCAN the next section for surface, traffic, weather, boundaries, and people.
PLAN a route, turnaround point, and trusted-adult contact before activity.
PACE so stopping and speaking comfortably remain possible.
TURN BACK before conditions, daylight, access, or control become unsafe.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Rehearse the model slowly, change one variable, and explain the cue or decision before adding complexity.

movementModel.title: Model for weather and hydration

movementModel.action: Scan the next section, choose a controlled route, state the help plan, and stop at the planned boundary.
movementModel.commonError: Choosing distance or destination before checking conditions and return options.

movementModel.notice: Notice route decisions, controlled stopping, and changing conditions rather than speed or distance.
movementModel.adaptedModel: Use the seated, supported, mobility-aid, reduced-range, object-modeled, or described route and preserve this evidence: Notice route decisions, controlled stopping, and changing conditions rather than speed or distance.
movementModel.safetyBoundary: Use a described indoor route unless a guardian has approved the real location, conditions, supervision, and activity-specific safety equipment. No real road, water, isolated area, unfamiliar route, or worsening weather is entered for lesson evidence.

independentActivity.title: Fresh application: weather and hydration
directions: Create or demonstrate a fresh route with a start, boundary, turnaround, condition check, and help plan.
Use this cue or decision: Scan, plan, pace, turn back.
Provide the selected evidence without a recording or body metric.
independentActivity.freshTask: Complete a fresh safe simulation or described plan with honest scope and guardian authority where required. Create or demonstrate a fresh route with a start, boundary, turnaround, condition check, and help plan.
independentActivity.independenceBoundary: A trusted human or future Tutor may read directions, define a cue, and offer an approved route. They may not perform the decision for the learner, claim unapproved observation, certify physical completion, or provide medical or return clearance.

warmUp: Trace the route slowly with a finger, hand, steps, or wheel pushes.
Rehearse one controlled stop and turnaround at comfortable range.
coolDown: Return to the easiest comfortable version or rest.
Restore optional equipment and space safely.
Name one cue, safety choice, or next adjustment without reporting body data.

spaceSetup: Clear one arm-span for an indoor route model. Real outdoor, road, water, isolated-area, or unfamiliar-route activity requires guardian permission and appropriate supervision/equipment. Low-space access remains available before and during the lesson. Cleanup: return optional items only after movement has stopped and the path is clear.

optional: Optional: paper map, weather-appropriate clothing, or activity-specific safety equipment when available and guardian-approved.
householdSubstitutes: Use a hand-drawn route, imaginary landmarks, or soft household markers indoors.
prohibited: No real road, water, isolated area, unfamiliar route, or worsening weather is entered for lesson evidence.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit low-space no-equipment route: point through an imaginary indoor route and explain the surface, weather, traffic, hydration, help, and turnaround decisions.

safetyRules: Check the surface, ceiling, boundary, people, pets, cords, breakables, footwear or mobility supports, and any optional item before movement.
Use a described indoor route unless a guardian has approved the real location, conditions, supervision, and activity-specific safety equipment.
Use learner-selected range, pace, and demand. Control, decisions, and understanding matter more than force, distance, duration, or repetitions.
If the environment cannot be made safe, do not perform movement; use the equal-credit described route or stop and tell a trusted adult.
stoppingRules: REST / ADJUST: You may pause, rest, reduce pace or range, use support, switch to an approved route, or finish for the day at any time. You may resume only when comfortable and the environment is safe. Rest and adaptation never reduce credit.

STOP AND TELL: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, an injury concern, damaged equipment, or an unsafe environment. Tell a trusted adult and do not continue to test the concern.

DO NOT RESUME: After a head impact, an injury concern, or a symptom that persists or worsens, remain out until the authorized guardian or qualified professional says it is safe. A learner, browser, or Tutor cannot provide clearance.

adaptationRoutes.seated: Use a stable seated position and preserve the Scan, plan, pace, turn back. evidence through upper-body movement, pointing, gesture, object modeling, or description.
adaptationRoutes.supported: Place an approved stable support before beginning and use it through the whole attempt; score the cue or decision for weather and hydration, not unsupported balance.
adaptationRoutes.reducedRange: Use the smallest comfortable movement, eye-gaze choice, point, or gesture that still shows the target cue or decision for weather and hydration.
adaptationRoutes.reducedPaceOrDemand: Complete one stage at a time with learner-chosen breaks, remain at the entry version, or split the lesson across short sittings.
adaptationRoutes.mobilityAidCompatible: Keep the mobility aid positioned and used as approved; adapt the path around the aid and score the same Scan, plan, pace, turn back. evidence.
adaptationRoutes.solo: Use the supplied solo, shadow, diagram, imagined-role, or fictional-situation route; no partner, opponent, group, or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.lowSpace: Use the one-arm-span or one-seat setup: Equal-credit low-space no-equipment route: point through an imaginary indoor route and explain the surface, weather, traffic, hydration, help, and turnaround decisions.
adaptationRoutes.noEquipment: Equal-credit low-space no-equipment route: point through an imaginary indoor route and explain the surface, weather, traffic, hydration, help, and turnaround decisions.
adaptationRoutes.describedOrDecisionRoute: Describe, draw, gesture, point, sign, or model Create or demonstrate a fresh route with a start, boundary, turnaround, condition check, and help plan. This is a complete equal-credit route when movement is not appropriate.

accessibleAdaptation: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice route decisions, controlled stopping, and changing conditions rather than speed or distance. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit low-space no-equipment route: point through an imaginary indoor route and explain the surface, weather, traffic, hydration, help, and turnaround decisions.
activitySteps: Choose a standard or equal-credit response route.
Read the STOP AND TELL rule.
Complete the warm-up when it applies.
Use the safe finish when it applies.
Answer the short reflection or leave it blank.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Choosing distance or destination before checking conditions and return options.

evidenceExpectations.observer: A learner may self-check a cue and a trusted human may review the selected evidence. A Tutor, browser, camera, wearable, or self-report cannot certify physical completion, guardian permission, or safe return.
doNotCollect: weight, appearance, body composition, calories, body shape, fitness norms, speed versus peers, or athletic talent
diagnosis, disability reason, symptom history, or private medical information
photo, video, audio, wearable data, location proof, or exercise log

retryPlan.trigger: Retry when the evidence does not yet show the target cue or decision for weather and hydration; name the missing observable part without judging the learner.
retryPlan.simplerSetup: Identify the safest start, boundary, and turnaround on a simple supplied route.
retryPlan.differentCue: Replace the full cue set with: “Scan, plan, pace, turn back.”
retryPlan.alternateModel: Contrast this common error — Choosing distance or destination before checking conditions and return options. — with this correction — Set the boundary and turnaround first; shorten or describe the route when conditions are uncertain.
retryPlan.boundedPractice: Travel, gesture, or point through one short clear segment and stop at the boundary.
retryPlan.freshRetry: Create or demonstrate a fresh route with a start, boundary, turnaround, condition check, and help plan. Use a new safe example rather than repeating the scored attempt.
retryPlan.exitCriterion: Return to independent work when the fresh retry shows or explains notice route decisions, controlled stopping, and changing conditions rather than speed or distance. A safety stop, rest, or adaptation is never recorded as failure.

guardianAuthority.when: Guardian permission is required before real movement, optional equipment, a real location, partner, outdoor route, or progression is used.
guardianAuthority.requiredAction: The guardian confirms that the bounded space, optional equipment, and activity route are permitted before movement.
guardianAuthority.minimumRecord: Record only permission status or that the equal-credit described route was used; collect no body, health, media, location, or performance data.
guardianAuthority.confirmationBoundary: Guardian confirmation may establish permission or occurrence only. It does not certify academic mastery, physical quality, diagnosis, effort, body status, or safe return.
guardianAuthority.equalCreditAlternative: When guardian review, real movement, equipment, space, partner, or location is unavailable, the supplied solo described/decision route is the complete equal-credit lesson.
